system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Cauchy-combined level-wise conformal few-shot evidence fused in log-odds with a temperature-calibrated zero-shot branch
SUMMARY: Replace the single fused few-shot conformal p-value with a Cauchy combination of the four level-wise conformal p-values, then fuse it with the temperature-calibrated zero-shot probability in log-odds as in the conformal parent.
HYPOTHESIS: Cauchy-combined level-wise few-shot p-values raise image AUROC by at least 0.5 points over a single fused few-shot p-value on held-out modalities while keeping the realised false-positive rate of the few-shot test within 2 points of 5%, and log-odds fusion with the calibrated zero-shot branch keeps AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline.
RATIONALE: The conformal parent treats each branch by its nature but collapses the few-shot branch's four levels into one score before the test; the Cauchy parent keeps level-wise evidence but treats the zero-shot softmax as another p-value, discarding its calibrated probability form. Combining them, the few-shot branch keeps its level-wise conformal p-values combined validly under dependence, and the zero-shot branch keeps its temperature-calibrated probability, each treated by its nature.
METHOD: 1) Few-shot: per level l, LOO support image scores r_i^l and test score s^l; p_l = (1 + #{r_i^l >= s^l})/(K + 1); Cauchy T = mean_l tan((0.5 - p_l) pi); p_fs = 0.5 - arctan(T)/pi. 2) Zero-shot: p0 with source-fitted temperature. 3) Fused logit z = w0 logit(p0) + w1 logit(1 - p_fs) + c, weights by logistic regression on source episodes. 4) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) single fused conformal p, (ii) Cauchy level-wise p, (iii) + log-odds fusion with calibrated zero-shot. Metrics: image AUROC, realised FPR at 0.05 for the few-shot test, ECE of the fused probability, score shift under resampling. Falsified if level-wise combination does not improve AUROC by 0.5 points or FPR exceeds 7%.

Idea B:
TITLE: Weight-free fusion of MVFA branches by a Bonferroni-corrected minimum p-value
SUMMARY: Replace inverse-variance fusion weights with a weight-free rule: convert each branch to a support-based conformal p-value and score the image by twice the smaller of the two, which is valid whatever the dependence between branches.
HYPOTHESIS: Bonferroni-min fusion matches support-reliability-weighted log-odds fusion within 0.5 image-AUROC points on held-out modalities, keeps the realised false-positive rate at or below the nominal 5%, and removes all fitted fusion parameters.
RATIONALE: The parent's framing is kept, fusion without source episodes, but inverse-variance weights estimated from K support images are themselves noisy at small K. The minimum p-value with a Bonferroni factor is the simplest valid combination of two tests under arbitrary dependence and needs no estimated weights; it lets whichever branch is more confident for a given image decide, which suits MVFA's complementary zero-shot (semantic) and few-shot (appearance) evidence.
METHOD: 1) Zero-shot branch: conformal p0 from LOO support scores of the temperature-calibrated softmax map (top-1% mean). 2) Few-shot branch: conformal p1 from LOO support scores. 3) p = min(1, 2 min(p0, p1)); score = -log10 p. 4) Threshold p <= 0.05. 5) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No training, no fitted fusion parameters.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: equal-weight log-odds; support-reliability weights (parent); Bonferroni-min; Simes combination (less conservative). Metrics: image AUROC, realised FPR at 0.05, score shift under resampling. Falsified if Bonferroni-min loses more than 0.5 AUROC points relative to the parent or exceeds nominal FPR.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>

CONFIDENCE: HIGH
